content.comment_body: I don't have experience with KNX and [product_name], but in [product_name] controller, at least when programmed with [product_name] and [version_no], you can only read 4 byte Float or 8 byte Double Float, as mentioned in the attached file. Are you sure about using a 2 byte Short Float?
Yes, [product_name] can exchange data using [product_name]. Is there another way to retrieve the network analog input? I attempted to use an F/I converter, but it was unsuccessful.

In your first image, you can see scaling from KNX value to [product_name] value. The second image displays an internal converter within [product_name], where the output value ranges between -32768 and +32767. This represents the [product_name] integer using 15 bits plus a sign bit. You might need to scale the value to obtain a usable thermostat reading. For example, a KNX value from 0.0 to 30.0 could be scaled to a [product_name] value from 0 to 300 (for one decimal) or 0 to 3000 (for two decimals).

You've set the [product_name] settings incorrectly. Channel 11 temperature from KNX should be mapped as -50:200 (KNX) -> 0:1000 ([product_name]). After that, you can use an analog amplifier for temperature normalization.

Why convert from -50:200 (KNX) to 0:1000 ([product_name]) and then use an analog amplifier with a gain of 2.50 and an offset of -500 in the [product_name] circuit? Wouldn't it be simpler to convert directly from -50:200 (KNX) to -500:2000 ([product_name]) and avoid using an amplifier?
I am not sure "why." It works for me, so I don't change it. Now I see that [article_no] and [article_no] duplicate themselves, and [article_no] is sufficient.
[user_name], thank you very much! I have reviewed my scheme, removed six extra blocks, and improved its readability!
